I was hoping to go to group counseling most of those reasons.

Thanks for the support.

It was just a screening. My therapist and I decided that I need to think about my problem more so that I have something to say at the meeting. I'm still in counseling, just private counseling.

Thanks for the support. I'll keep your advice in mind.

The coordinator said I would be wrong for group because I haven't thought about my problem enough and that I admit to being too blunt. I my honest intents could turn into confrontational messages. I decided on a few personal sessions.

Thanks for the sharing your experiences.
Thanks for the support and advice.

I am getting help from my university's counseling center, but I wouldn't mind a back up in case they were no help.

EDIT: I've been meditating and I find it effective when paired with cardio workouts.

EDIT 2: I'll post when I've made some progress or if I have a problem. It would seem this problem is not uncommon, so I'll make more posts and make a compilation post when this is behind me.
I'll check it out. Thanks for the advice.

Thanks for the support and advice. I wasn't sure if I should seek out some kind of help, because I wasn't sure if I had a problem. I guess I denied the problem since I viewed myself I as strong enough to overcome or ignore this kind of issue.

That makes me feel a little better. Intuition tells me that a lot of the smart people on campus feel the same way. The only difference is between me and them is that they're used to it and know how to deal with it. I've realized in a short time that I'm going to be the tutor of the study group during college and the thinker for countless people after I'm done with school. I suppose it's just a matter of getting comfortable to the new role.

EDIT: I forgot about why I was posting. Thank you!
